Throwaways serve an important function on Reddit but it seems unnecessarily cumbersome for people to need to create a whole other account to post things in a manner that minimizes the risk of it being tracked back to them.

I know some people have inquired about anonymous settings for various aspects of the site with varying degrees of reception but I think there might be some value in a "throwaway" setting for posts that obfuscate things in a way that is at least as anonymizing as a throwaway account.

Thoughts?

Edit: Maybe there could be one sitewide primary ThrowAway account and when users tag their post with the throwaway option it gets posted under that accounts name, with options to report for abuse if someone is just spamming or using it in an absurd or irrelevant fashion not inline with its intent, if someone abuses it too much they cant use the function for X amount of time or something like that.

IMO, this notion of "privacy" is one of the more important concepts we have a name for. Therefore, if anyone is going to make any attempt at anonymity while interacting with any website, they have to effectively "trick" any humans and computer hardware that they are a unique user. As such, the only way to accomplish actual anonymity is to visit any site (and make user accounts, etc.) in such away that draws no connection to your "non-anonymous" identity. To be more brief, you must at the very least appear to be using a different computer, from a different IP address, with different username, and so on. And this is assuming the site you're visiting isn't using any clever profiling algorithm with sneaky data points like many of them do (such as the version of your browser, the OS you're using and it's version, the size of the window, and others).

With that said, it's important users realize that while their username is obfuscated in subs that enable anonymous mode, their actual username is known to voat. The feature put forward in the OP would be the same. The point here being that, while voat may not care about what some user number says in an anon sub, a law enforcement authority that seizes voat's database in the distant future might. Caveat emptor.

So yeah, if what you want is actual anonymity, you have to at least make a throwaway.

Well, yea. But I didn't even bother worrying about that level of security and anonymity because if someone is going to be that proactive and that serious about it then throw aways are going to be the least of what they do to hide themselves.

I was thinking more along the lines of general life stuff that people might want to tell stories about but might not want associated with their main account /user name

Oh yes, sure. I do see your point, and I do find it valid. I would say then, perhaps simply allowing users to choose the same obfuscation as they get in the anon subs should do it.

In anon subs, votes only count for placement. With a feature like this, switching to anon mode in non anon subs should not be a way to avoid getting downvoats.

Usually the reason people use a throwaway though is just because they don't want that post publicly connected to their account. They typically don't mind Voat/Reddit knowing which account the post is linked to. In this case, an anonymity/throwaway mode would be great and eliminate the need for throwaway accounts.

I think a good and potentially easy solution to this problem would be to modify Voat's database so that there is a flag for throwaway posts. If a post is flagged as a throwaway, the username is publicly redacted but otherwise everything is the same. This should be both relatively simple to implement and would offer a great solution to the issue of anonymized posts.

The only problem with this solution is when things go wrong and the username isn't redacted. If we're talking about a spammer/troll I'm sure nobody would complain too much, but there are some topics I won't touch with a 10' pole on this account. I'm going to leave absolutely nothing to chance when I'm commenting on something I'm actually interested in, but don't want traced back to me. More than that, should somebody go on a doxxing spree targeting anybody that has posted on some hot topic I don't want this name dragged through the mud.

From my perspective throwaways will always have a place, and they will become even more vital to those concerned about their privacy until doxxing/swatting doesn't happen anymore.
What do you mean by "when things go wrong"?

A site I frequent for humorous stories related to retail, Not Always Right, allows for user submission of stories. Contact information for the users submitting the stories is not for public consumption, but on more than one occasion I have seen it show up in submissions. I have also seen various database errors in the same area of each story.

Now, anybody that's worked in retail knows that the average customer is an idiot. One can make that extension to people submitting their stories and assume that some people manage to put their email addresses in a blank they don't mean to. However, that's just an assumption with no real way of knowing if it really was user error or not. I choose to presume that it's the scripts bugging out somehow. Were I to post something that I truly wanted to remain disconnected from this identity I am not going to put my faith in a program that could go wrong at any given moment and not give me the anonymity that I need, no matter how minute the chance.
